concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: The original Section 8.1 of the DPA requires notification within 48 hours, and the amendment replacing it only takes effect on 1 October 2026, after 15 September 2026.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment A2.1 replaces Section 8.1 with a 24-hour outer limit, effective 1 October 2026 and therefore in force on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment A3.1 reduces the on-site audit notice period under Section 10.2 from 30 days to 20 days, effective from 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment A6.1 replaces Section 13.1 with a fixed Processor aggregate liability cap of EUR 1,000,000, which is in force from 1 October 2026 and does not depend on fees paid.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: Amendment A6.1 expressly provides that the EUR 1,000,000 cap shall not apply to breaches of Section 4 (Confidentiality).

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed in Annex 3 as an approved Sub-processor, and its withdrawal only takes effect on 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: Amendment A4.1 withdraws approval of Meridian Mail Ltd with effect from 1 January 2027, and the later emergency permission is limited to incident IR-27 in May 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, the approved processing locations are Norway (existing storage), Estonia (Skylark Hosting), Lithuania (Baltika Analytics), France (Cendrillon Mail) and Denmark (Dagmar Backup), with Ireland excluded after Meridian's withdrawal.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: Under amended Section 12.1, deletion or return is due within 60 days of termination, so counting from 31 December 2026 (excluding the trigger date) gives 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting personal data processed under the dpa, with the required notice content unchanged.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting personal data processed under the DPA, with the required notice content unchanged.
justifications: Amendment A2.1 sets the 24-hour outer limit in force from 1 October 2026, and A2.2 confirms the Section 8.2 content requirements remain unchanged.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: Breach was confirmed to expose usable privileged credentials, so the 12-hour expedited outer limit applies from the original awareness at 17:10 on 9 April 2027. The clause applies even though the exposure was confirmed later.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: The 12-hour expedited limit from awareness at 17:10 on 9 April 2027 expired at 05:10 on 10 April, and the first notice was delivered at 06:00, 50 minutes later.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: Counting from awareness on 9 April, the 12 April closure is skipped and 14 April is excluded as the only approved pause day, so the third Business Day is 16 April 2027.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: Held records are released when the last hold ends on 25 August 2027. The deletion deadline is the later of the 60-day ordinary deadline (29 August 2027) and the end of the tenth Business Day after release, which is 9 September 2027.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: BK-0630 was created on 30 June 2027 and contains no held records, so it must be deleted by the earlier of its ordinary deadline and 35 calendar days after creation. The 35-day limit yields 4 August 2027, which is earlier than the 60-day ordinary deadline.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: After the ordinary deletion deadline, the hold and its following deletion window remain the sole retention authority, and records retained solely under a legal hold may be used only for legal preservation. Service delivery and analytics uses are excluded, and an analytics retention request was rejected.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval for a new or expanded service starts no earlier than the latest of the proposed start date, completion of the security review, and written Controller consent. For the Stockholm infrastructure service, the security review completed on 22 April, which is later than the 20 April start date and the 18 April consent.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd's approval was withdrawn from 1 January 2027 and its emergency permission covers only incident IR-27 until 11 May 2027, so it is not authorised for ordinary email on 10 May 2027. Cendrillon Mail SAS was added for transactional email from 1 January 2027 and continues in that role.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: These countries have actual processing and effective authorisation on 15 May 2027: Norway and Estonia for storage and infrastructure, Lithuania for monitoring, France for transactional email, and Sweden for Stockholm infrastructure. Denmark and Ireland lost authorisation before that date, and Finland and Germany have no effective authorisation or processing.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: The security cap is the greater of EUR 2,000,000 and twice Qualifying Fees. Qualifying Fees of EUR 1,140,000 (EUR 1,200,000 excluding VAT, less the EUR 60,000 service credit) give twice that amount, EUR 2,280,000.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year, and EUR 300,000 of ordinary payments have already been made in the current Contract Year, leaving EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: Ordinary claim C-1 is capped at the remaining EUR 700,000 ordinary pool. Security loss L-2 of EUR 1,750,000 fits within the remaining security pool of EUR 1,780,000, and confidentiality-precedence losses L-3 (EUR 250,000) and L-4 (EUR 100,000) are uncapped, totaling EUR 2,800,000.
